supplements.name: Bell's Palsy (Facial Nerve Paralysis)
supplements.notes: Onset December 2024. As of September 2026 (~21 months), face is not notably droopy — just slightly — but there is an extreme downward pressure sensation, like someone pulling downward on the face. Bell's palsy is acute peripheral facial nerve (CN VII) paralysis, usually caused by viral reactivation (HSV-1 or VZV) and/or inflammation compressing the nerve within the bony fallopian canal of the temporal bone.

supplements.name: Elevated CRP (C-Reactive Protein)
supplements.notes: Lab confirmed 9/15/2026 (Quest): CRP 74.8 mg/L (ref <8.0), ESR 56 mm/h (ref ≤30). Extremely elevated — normal CRP is <3 mg/L. WBC is normal (9.7), arguing against active bacterial infection. CALCIUM is 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH, ref 8.6-10.4) — confirms D3-induced hypercalcemia. eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60) — Stage 3a kidney disease, likely from hypercalcemia. The high calcium is likely driving CRP via NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Hemoglobin 12.8 and hematocrit 38.7 are low-normal for a male, consistent with anemia of chronic inflammation.

supplements.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS)
supplements.notes: Autoimmune inflammatory disease primarily attacking the spine and sacroiliac joints. Causes chronic pain, stiffness, and can fuse vertebrae. AS drives chronically elevated CRP and ESR through autoimmune inflammation. Currently treating with high-dose D3 (Coimbra Protocol approach) — a real medical protocol using 40,000-200,000 IU D3 to suppress the overactive immune system. The protocol REQUIRES: (1) strict low-calcium diet — NO dairy, no pizza, no calcium-fortified foods, (2) 2.5L+ water daily to flush calcium through kidneys, (3) regular bloodwork every 3-6 months, (4) supervision by a Coimbra-trained physician. Current labs (9/15/2026) show these supporting measures are not in place: calcium 11.3 (HIGH), eGFR 53 (kidney damage). Find a Coimbra-trained doctor at CoimbraProtocol.com or through Coimbra Protocol Facebook groups.

interactions.title: Multiple Antiplatelet Agents: Bleeding Risk
interactions.description: This stack layers blood-thinning mechanisms: krill oil (omega-3s), black seed oil (1,000 mg — antihypertensive/antiplatelet), astaxanthin (mild antiplatelet), and curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo — antiplatelet and anti-coagulant with BioPerine boosting absorption up to 2,000%). With the NMN combo removed (resveratrol and quercetin no longer in the stack) and black seed oil halved, the antiplatelet load is reduced but still meaningful.
interactions.recommendation: Antiplatelet load is lower with NMN combo removed and black seed oil reduced. Coimbra physician should know about the full antiplatelet stack before any surgery or dental procedures.

interactions.title: D3 Reduced to ~42,800 IU: Monitoring Hypercalcemia & Kidney Recovery
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026 (at prior dose of ~102,800 IU/day): Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH, ref 8.6-10.4), eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60 — Stage 3a kidney disease), BUN 26 (HIGH), Creatinine 1.16 (HIGH). D3 has since been REDUCED to ~42,800 IU/day (40,000 standalone + 2,800 from multi/Protaflo) with K2 reduced to ~6,580 mcg. Now under Coimbra physician supervision with dairy-free diet and 2.5L+ water daily in place. The protocol requirements are being met: (1) strict low-calcium diet (dairy-free), (2) 2.5+ liters of water daily, (3) regular bloodwork, (4) Coimbra physician supervision. Awaiting follow-up labs to confirm the dose reduction and dietary compliance are resolving the hypercalcemia and kidney damage.
interactions.recommendation: Protocol compliance is now in place. Recheck calcium, eGFR, and 25(OH)D in 4-6 weeks to confirm the dose reduction and dietary compliance are working. If calcium normalizes and eGFR improves, the current dose may be appropriate long-term under physician guidance. Continue K2 at current dose.

interactions.title: Iodine Intake at 600 mcg: ~4x RDA, Monitor Thyroid
interactions.description: 600 mcg of iodine is about 4x the RDA (150 mcg), still below the upper tolerable limit (1,100 mcg) but getting meaningful. The multivitamin adds ~15 mg (likely listed as 15 mcg based on label) of additional iodine. At this dose, there is a real risk of thyroid disruption in people with underlying thyroid conditions — both hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's) and hyperthyroidism (Graves') can be triggered or worsened by iodine supplementation above 500 mcg. The Wolff-Chaikoff effect (transient hypothyroidism from iodine excess) is a concern at this level.
interactions.recommendation: Still below the UL but warrants thyroid function monitoring (TSH, free T4). Watch for symptoms of thyroid dysfunction: fatigue, weight changes, temperature sensitivity, or heart rate changes. If thyroid issues exist, this dose may be too high.

interactions.title: Multiple Natural BP-Lowering Agents
interactions.description: Several supplements in this stack lower blood pressure through different mechanisms: magnesium (vasodilator, ~209 mg elemental), potassium (1,020 mg — counteracts sodium), moringa (BP-lowering), and black seed oil (1,000 mg — antihypertensive). These natural agents are individually mild but together create a meaningful BP-lowering combination, especially when fasting or dehydrated.
interactions.recommendation: Much safer without tadalafil. Still worth monitoring blood pressure, especially when combining moringa and black seed oil. Watch for dizziness when getting up quickly.

interactions.title: Multiple Mild Blood-Sugar-Lowering Agents
interactions.description: Several supplements have mild blood-sugar-lowering effects: moringa, black seed oil, chromium (40 mcg from multi), and ALCAR. Individually these are minor, but together they create a moderate glucose-lowering stack, especially when fasting or exercising.
interactions.recommendation: Low risk without the dedicated blood sugar formula and berberine. Monitor if diabetic or on glucose-lowering medication.

interactions.title: Iron Absorption Competed by Minerals
interactions.description: The Codeage multi contains iron (27.5 mg). Zinc (~22.5 mg total from multi 7.5 mg + Protaflo 15 mg), calcium, and magnesium all compete with iron for absorption. Protaflo's curcumin (200 mg with BioPerine) also chelates iron. Magnesium and calcium add further competition. With standalone zinc removed, zinc competition is reduced but still present.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron 2+ hours away from zinc-containing supplements (multi, Protaflo), calcium, and magnesium. Or take iron with vitamin C to enhance absorption.

interactions.title: Synergistic: D3 + K2 + Magnesium
interactions.description: This is a well-designed synergistic combination. K2 directs D3-mobilized calcium to bones and away from arteries. Magnesium is required for D3 metabolism (converts D3 to active 1,25-dihydroxy form). However, the D3 dose itself is the concern — the support stack is good.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination — just address the D3 dose.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Complete B-Vitamin Coverage
interactions.description: The standalone B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B12) plus those in the multivitamin provide thorough B-complex coverage. B vitamins work synergistically and are water-soluble (excess is excreted). Benfotiamine (B1) and P5P (B6) are superior bioavailable forms. Methylcobalamin (B12) is the active form. This is a well-constructed B-vitamin protocol.
interactions.recommendation: Good selection of forms. Monitor B6 total intake — keep under 100 mg/day long-term to avoid neuropathy.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Vitamin C recycles oxidized glutathione back to its active reduced form. Liposomal glutathione has better absorption than standard. This is a solid antioxidant foundation.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination for antioxidant support.

interactions.title: Magnesium from 3 Sources: ~209 mg Elemental
interactions.description: Magnesium from 3 sources: L-threonate (~144 mg elemental), glycinate (~50 mg), multi (15 mg). Total supplemental elemental Mg ~209 mg, well within the 350 mg UL from supplements. Well-distributed across bioavailable forms.
interactions.recommendation: Spread magnesium doses throughout the day. Total is within safe range.

interactions.title: CoQ10 from 2 Sources: ~25 mg Supplemental

interactions.recommendation: CoQ10 at this level is beneficial. No concerns.

interactions.title: Rhodiola + Saffron: Serotonin & Dopamine Overlap
interactions.description: Rhodiola rosea increases serotonin and dopamine by inhibiting MAO enzymes. Saffron also affects serotonin reuptake (similar mechanism to SSRIs). Together they create a mild serotonergic combination. If combined with any antidepressant medication, there is a risk of serotonin syndrome — symptoms include agitation, rapid heartbeat, high temperature, and muscle twitching.
interactions.recommendation: Safe together at these doses for most people, but do NOT combine with SSRI/SNRI antidepressants without physician approval.

interactions.title: Synergistic: TMG + B12 + Folate Methylation Support
interactions.description: TMG (trimethylglycine) donates methyl groups to convert homocysteine to methionine. B12 (5,000 mcg) and folate (from the multi) support the same pathway via a different route. Together they provide comprehensive methylation support — important for DNA repair, detox, cardiovascular health, and myelin synthesis for Bell's palsy nerve repair. The increased B12 dose makes this methylation support robust.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent synergy, especially for nerve repair. The TMG dose is appropriate for the high B12.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Astaxanthin + Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Astaxanthin is one of the most potent antioxidants found in nature, working in both water- and fat-soluble environments. Combined with glutathione (the body's master antioxidant) and vitamin C (which recycles glutathione), this trio provides excellent multi-layer antioxidant protection.
interactions.recommendation: Strong antioxidant combination. Astaxanthin at 12 mg is a well-studied, safe dose.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: Hypercalcemia (11.3) Worsening Bell's Palsy Symptoms
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026 (at prior dose of ~102,800 IU/day): Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH). D3 has since been reduced to ~42,800 IU/day. The 'extreme downward pressure' sensation at 21 months now has a likely explanation. Calcium is the trigger for muscle contraction — at 11.3 mg/dL, excess calcium causes continuous low-grade contraction and muscle hypertonicity in ALL muscles, but the damaged facial nerve side is most vulnerable. The facial nerve (CN VII) controls the muscles of facial expression — calcium dysregulation at the neuromuscular junction directly produces abnormal muscle tone, contracture (synkinesis), and the 'pulling downward' sensation. Additionally, high calcium drives systemic inflammation (CRP 74.8) maintaining nerve compression within the bony fallopian canal. At the prior dose, D3 was causing a triple hit: (1) hypercalcemia-driven muscle dysfunction, (2) inflammation-driven nerve compression, (3) kidney damage (eGFR 53) reducing waste clearance.
interactions.recommendation: D3 HAS BEEN REDUCED from ~102,800 to ~42,800 IU/day. As calcium normalizes, expect: less facial pressure, reduced muscle hypertonicity, lower CRP (less nerve inflammation), and improved kidney function. Strict dietary calcium restriction and 2.5L+ water daily are essential for the dose reduction to work. This is the most treatable cause of the persistent symptoms.

interactions.title: Synergistic: B Vitamins + Lion's Mane + ALCAR + Magnesium — Nerve Repair Arsenal
interactions.description: This is the strongest nerve-repair combination in the stack. B12 methylcobalamin (5,000 mcg — increased to therapeutic dose) is critical for myelin synthesis and nerve regeneration — the single most important supplement for Bell's palsy recovery. Lion's Mane (1,000 mg) stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) — directly promotes nerve regeneration and remyelination, making it one of the most targeted supplements for Bell's palsy. B1 benfotiamine (600 mg) supports nerve energy metabolism and reduces neuroinflammation — the doubled dose strengthens this nerve support significantly. B2 riboflavin (400 mg) supports mitochondrial function in nerve cells. B6 P5P (25 mg) supports neurotransmitter synthesis needed for nerve signaling. ALCAR (1,500 mg) crosses the blood-brain barrier and directly supports nerve regeneration and mitochondrial function in nerve cells. Magnesium L-threonate crosses the blood-brain barrier and is neuroprotective. For Bell's palsy recovery at 21 months, this combination actively supports facial nerve regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent foundation for nerve recovery. B12 is now at therapeutic 5,000 mcg — good for active nerve healing. B1 benfotiamine doubled to 600 mg — strong support for nerve energy metabolism. Lion's Mane is the most targeted NGF stimulator available. Keep total B6 under 100 mg/day (currently ~35 mg total including multi — safe). These are the most important supplements to keep taking.

interactions.title: Anti-Inflammatory Agents May Reduce Residual Facial Nerve Edema
interactions.description: The facial nerve runs through the narrow fallopian canal in the temporal bone. Any swelling compresses the nerve. The persistent 'extreme downward pressure' at 21 months suggests residual inflammation or nerve edema. The anti-inflammatory agents include: thymoquinone (black seed oil 1,000 mg), omega-3s (krill oil), and curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo with BioPerine for enhanced absorption). Curcumin is one of the strongest natural anti-inflammatory agents for nerve edema reduction.
interactions.recommendation: Protaflo's curcumin + BioPerine provides meaningful anti-inflammatory support for facial nerve edema. Black seed oil's thymoquinone adds NF-kB inhibition.

interactions.title: Mild Vasodilators May Support Facial Nerve Blood Supply
interactions.description: Bell's palsy involves ischemia (reduced blood flow) of the facial nerve compressed within the bony fallopian canal. Improving blood supply could aid recovery even at 21 months — nerve regeneration is slow (~1 mm/day). Magnesium is a vasodilator (~209 mg elemental from 3 sources), and moringa (1,000 mg) lowers blood pressure. With tadalafil removed from the stack, the remaining vasodilation effect is mild but still present.
interactions.recommendation: Mild vasodilation from magnesium and moringa. Without tadalafil, the hypotension risk is minimal and the nerve blood supply benefit is modest.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Glutathione + Antioxidants Protect Recovering Nerve Cells
interactions.description: Damaged nerve cells generate excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) during recovery, which can further damage the nerve if unchecked. This antioxidant combination provides multi-layer protection: glutathione (master intracellular antioxidant — 500 mg liposomal), vitamin C (recycles glutathione, extracellular protection — 500 mg), astaxanthin (crosses blood-brain barrier, 6,000x more potent than vitamin C — 12 mg), and TMG (supports methylation critical for myelin synthesis — 1,500 mg). For a facial nerve recovering from Bell's palsy, oxidative damage is a key barrier to regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Strong foundation for nerve recovery. Astaxanthin's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier makes it especially valuable for facial nerve protection. TMG's methylation support is critical for myelin repair.

interactions.title: Selenium from 2 Sources: 275 mcg Total
interactions.description: Selenium from 2 sources: multivitamin 75 mcg + Protaflo 200 mcg = 275 mcg total. The upper tolerable limit is 400 mcg/day, and this intake is at 69% of the UL. Selenium is essential for thyroid function and antioxidant defense but chronic excess causes selenosis (hair loss, brittle nails, GI distress, neurological symptoms). Both sources use L-selenomethionine, the most bioavailable form.
interactions.recommendation: 275 mcg is safe but getting closer to the UL. Avoid additional selenium-rich foods in high quantities (Brazil nuts are extremely high — one nut can contain 70-90 mcg). Monitor for selenosis symptoms if dose increases.

interactions.title: BioPerine/Piperine: 5 mg from Protaflo
interactions.description: Piperine (BioPerine) at 5 mg from Protaflo inhibits CYP3A4 and other drug-metabolizing enzymes, slowing the clearance of many compounds. The main practical effect: curcumin absorption increases up to 2,000% with piperine (a designed feature of Protaflo). With the NMN combo removed, piperine load is halved from the previous 10 mg.
interactions.recommendation: Piperine load is lower with only Protaflo as a source. If any prescription medication is added, inform the Coimbra physician about the 5 mg piperine — it affects the metabolism of many drugs.

interactions.title: Anti-Inflammatory Stack May Help Lower CRP from 75 mg/L
interactions.description: CRP at ~75 mg/L indicates severe systemic inflammation (normal <3 mg/L). This stack contains evidence-based CRP-lowering agents: curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo with BioPerine enhancing absorption up to 2,000%) — meta-analyses show curcumin significantly reduces CRP; thymoquinone (black seed oil 1,000 mg) — clinical trials show CRP reduction; omega-3 fatty acids (krill oil 2,000 mg) — strong evidence for lowering CRP, especially EPA. Together these attack inflammation through NF-κB inhibition, COX-2 reduction, and cytokine suppression. With D3 reduced and dietary compliance in place, the CRP should begin dropping from both the supplement anti-inflammatory action and reduced hypercalcemia-driven inflammation.
interactions.recommendation: These anti-inflammatory supplements are critically important given CRP at 75. Curcumin + BioPerine is the strongest agent here. The D3 reduction and dietary calcium elimination should address the hypercalcemia-driven CRP component. The Coimbra Protocol D3 at proper dose with compliance should help address the AS-driven component. Recheck CRP in 4-6 weeks.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: D3 → High Calcium → High CRP → Persistent Bell's Palsy (The Chain)
interactions.description: Labs confirmed the chain: D3 at ~102,800 IU/day (since reduced to ~42,800) → calcium 11.3 (HIGH) → NLRP3 inflammasome activation → CRP 74.8 → ongoing inflammation compressing the facial nerve at 21 months. HOWEVER, ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is ALSO driving CRP independently — AS is an autoimmune inflammatory disease that produces elevated CRP and ESR as part of its disease activity. The CRP of 74.8 likely reflects BOTH sources: D3-induced hypercalcemia AND AS autoimmune inflammation. The persistent Bell's palsy is being actively maintained by inflammation from TWO sources — supplement-driven (fixable by reducing D3) and autoimmune (requires AS treatment). Normal WBC (9.7) rules out infection. ESR at 56 confirms chronic inflammation. Most Bell's palsy resolves in 3-6 months — this one hasn't because inflammation from both D3 and AS hasn't been controlled.
interactions.recommendation: Reducing D3 should significantly lower CRP, but may not normalize it completely because AS itself drives inflammation. The path forward requires addressing BOTH sources: (1) reduce D3 or properly implement Coimbra Protocol with dietary restrictions to fix hypercalcemia, (2) work with a rheumatologist or Coimbra physician to manage AS disease activity. MRI with gadolinium can confirm active nerve inflammation.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: D3-Induced Hypercalcemia (11.3) Driving CRP of 74.8
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026 (at prior dose of ~102,800 IU/day): Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH). D3 has since been reduced to ~42,800 IU/day. At the prior dose, D3 pushed calcium above the safe range despite ~6,580 mcg K2. High calcium activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, which drives IL-1β production, which triggers CRP production in the liver. This was likely a major contributor to the CRP of 74.8. The normal WBC (9.7) argues against infection, making the hypercalcemia-driven inflammatory pathway the main driver. The dose reduction should lower calcium → reduce NLRP3 activation → lower IL-1β → lower CRP.
interactions.recommendation: D3 has been reduced from ~102,800 to ~42,800 IU/day. This is the single most impactful change for lowering CRP. Calcium should begin normalizing within weeks. Recheck calcium, CRP, and eGFR in 4-6 weeks to confirm the cascade is reversing. Strict dietary calcium restriction is essential for the dose reduction to work.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Antioxidant Defense Against Inflammatory Oxidative Damage
interactions.description: CRP at 75 mg/L means massive oxidative stress — inflammation generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) that damage tissues, proteins, and DNA. This antioxidant combination provides multi-layer protection: glutathione (500 mg liposomal — the body's master intracellular antioxidant, directly neutralizes ROS), vitamin C (500 mg — extracellular antioxidant, recycles glutathione back to active form), and astaxanthin (12 mg — crosses the blood-brain barrier, 6,000x more potent than vitamin C, protects cell membranes). With CRP this high, oxidative damage is ongoing and cumulative. These antioxidants won't lower CRP directly, but they protect tissues from the collateral damage of chronic inflammation.
interactions.recommendation: Important protective role given the extreme inflammation. These antioxidants are especially valuable for protecting the recovering facial nerve from oxidative damage caused by the systemic inflammation. Keep these in the stack.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Methylation Support Lowers Homocysteine-Driven Inflammation
interactions.description: Elevated homocysteine is an independent driver of inflammation and raises CRP. TMG (1,500 mg) donates methyl groups to convert homocysteine to methionine via BHMT pathway. B12 methylcobalamin (5,000 mcg) and folate (from multi) support the parallel MTHFR pathway. Together they provide comprehensive homocysteine-lowering support. While homocysteine is unlikely to be the primary cause of a CRP this high, it could be a contributing factor. This methylation support helps keep one inflammatory pathway in check.
interactions.recommendation: Check homocysteine levels as part of the inflammatory workup. This methylation trio is well-designed and provides modest CRP benefit.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: Stage 3a Kidney Disease (eGFR 53) from Hypercalcemia
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026 (at prior dose of ~102,800 IU/day): eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60), BUN 26 (HIGH, ref 7-25), Creatinine 1.16 (HIGH, ref 0.50-1.05). This is Stage 3a chronic kidney disease. The most likely cause is hypercalcemia (calcium 11.3) from the prior D3 dose — excess calcium deposits in renal tubules (nephrocalcinosis). D3 has since been reduced to ~42,800 IU/day. With reduced kidney function, several supplements need attention: potassium (1,020 mg — serum K is 4.5, normal for now, but damaged kidneys struggle to excrete potassium); magnesium (~209 mg elemental — reduced clearance increases risk of hypermagnesemia). The kidney damage is likely REVERSIBLE if calcium normalizes with the reduced dose — Stage 3a caught early has a good prognosis.
interactions.recommendation: D3 has been reduced from ~102,800 to ~42,800 IU/day. Monitor potassium and magnesium levels since kidney clearance is reduced. Stage 3a is reversible if calcium normalizes quickly. Recheck eGFR, BUN, creatinine, and calcium in 4-6 weeks to confirm kidney recovery. Strict dietary calcium restriction and 2.5L+ water daily are essential. If eGFR continues to decline, nephrology referral is needed.

interactions.title: Coimbra Protocol for AS: High-Dose D3 Requires Strict Dietary Compliance
interactions.description: The ~42,800 IU D3 (40,000 standalone) is an intentional Coimbra Protocol approach for ankylosing spondylitis — a legitimate medical protocol that uses 40,000-200,000 IU D3 to suppress autoimmune activity. D3 was reduced from ~102,800 IU to address lab-confirmed hypercalcemia and kidney damage. The protocol requirements are now being met: (1) dairy-free diet eliminating primary calcium sources, (2) 2.5+ liters of water daily to flush calcium through the kidneys, (3) Coimbra-trained physician supervision with regular bloodwork. Labs at the prior dose (calcium 11.3, eGFR 53) prompted these corrective steps. Awaiting follow-up labs to confirm improvement.
interactions.recommendation: Protocol compliance is now in place with dairy-free diet, high water intake, and Coimbra physician supervision. The dose reduction from ~102,800 to ~42,800 IU/day combined with proper dietary compliance should allow calcium to normalize and kidneys to recover. Recheck calcium, eGFR, PTH, and 25(OH)D in 4-6 weeks. The Coimbra physician will adjust the dose based on lab results — the current 40,000 IU standalone may be increased if labs improve with proper compliance.

interactions.title: AS Drives CRP Independently — D3 Reduction Alone May Not Normalize It
interactions.description: The CRP of 74.8 has TWO drivers: (1) D3-induced hypercalcemia activating the NLRP3 inflammasome (fixable by reducing D3/fixing diet), and (2) ankylosing spondylitis autoimmune inflammation (requires disease management). CRP levels of 20-80+ mg/L are common during active AS flares — the AS alone could account for much of the elevation. This means even after D3 is reduced and calcium normalizes, the CRP may remain elevated if AS is in an active flare. The high CRP in turn drives: persistent Bell's palsy (nerve inflammation), kidney stress (inflammatory load on already-damaged kidneys), and general tissue damage. The Coimbra Protocol aims to address the AS component by suppressing autoimmune activity with D3, but at the current unsupervised dose, it's causing MORE inflammation through hypercalcemia than it's preventing through immune suppression.
interactions.recommendation: Both prongs are now being addressed: (1) D3 reduced and dairy-free diet + high water in place to resolve hypercalcemia-driven inflammation, (2) Coimbra Protocol under physician supervision to manage AS disease activity. Track CRP at each lab draw to see which component is improving. If CRP remains high after calcium normalizes, the AS is the remaining driver and the Coimbra physician may adjust the D3 dose upward with verified dietary compliance.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Anti-Inflammatory Stack Therapeutic for AS Spinal Inflammation
interactions.description: The anti-inflammatory supplements in this stack are especially important for ankylosing spondylitis. Curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo + BioPerine for enhanced absorption) is one of the most studied natural anti-inflammatories for AS — clinical trials show it reduces TNF-alpha and CRP in AS patients. Omega-3s (krill oil 2,000 mg) reduce IL-6 and CRP. Thymoquinone (black seed oil 1,000 mg) inhibits NF-κB, a central driver of AS inflammation. With echinacea and elderberry removed, the stack is no longer working against itself — all remaining supplements suppress rather than stimulate inflammation, complementing the Coimbra Protocol.
interactions.recommendation: These are among the most important supplements to KEEP in the stack for AS. Curcumin with BioPerine is the standout. The anti-inflammatory stack works alongside the Coimbra Protocol approach — suppressing inflammation while D3 modulates autoimmune activity.

interactions.title: AS + Bell's Palsy: Autoimmune Crossover — Two Targets, One Immune System
interactions.description: Ankylosing spondylitis proves his immune system attacks his own tissues. The persistence of Bell's palsy at 21 months — far beyond the typical 3-6 month recovery — now has an additional explanation beyond hypercalcemia. Autoimmune inflammation from AS may be contributing to facial nerve damage through several mechanisms: (1) systemic autoimmune inflammation affecting multiple nerve targets (AS patients have higher rates of cranial nerve involvement), (2) the same inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6) that attack spinal joints also damage peripheral nerves, (3) the immune system primed to attack self-tissue may target the facial nerve within the fallopian canal. The combination of AS and persistent Bell's palsy suggests a broader autoimmune phenotype — one in which the immune system has multiple tissue targets. This makes immune STIMULATION (echinacea) even more dangerous and immune MODULATION even more important.
interactions.recommendation: An immunologist or neurologist should evaluate whether AS and Bell's palsy share an autoimmune mechanism — this could fundamentally change treatment for both. The Coimbra Protocol now under physician supervision may help both conditions if they share an autoimmune mechanism. The nerve repair stack (B12, lion's mane, ALCAR, benfotiamine) remains critical regardless of cause.
